summary: The France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship is a French government programme created by the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs and run by Campus France. It helps French higher education institutions attract top international students to master's, engineering and doctoral programmes, in seven priority thematic areas, to train future decision-makers from outside France. Students cannot apply themselves: a French institution must choose the candidate and submit the application. The award gives a monthly allowance plus services such as travel, insurance and housing help, but it does not pay tuition or course fees.
eligibility_notes:
The programme is for international students. Only French higher education institutions (and national research organisations) can submit applications; applications sent by students or by foreign institutions are declared ineligible. The student first talks to a Campus France office or the cultural and cooperation service of a French embassy, and to the international relations office of a French institution, which must accept the candidate and then submit the file online.

Age: up to 29 years for master's candidates and up to 35 years for doctoral candidates.

Programme types that can be nominated: a master's degree (or equivalent) accredited by the French state, a nationally accredited engineering programme, or a doctoral programme under joint supervision or as a dual degree with a partner institution abroad. Only programmes that confer a nationally accredited degree are allowed. French programmes located abroad are not accepted. Programmes under an apprenticeship or professionalisation contract are ineligible. The host institution commits to enrol the awardee in the programme for which they were selected.

Master's level: candidates who are already studying in France are ineligible.

Doctoral level: students currently studying abroad have priority over those who live in France. A 36-month award is reserved for first-year PhD students registering in France for the first time.

Current recipients of a French government scholarship are not eligible; however, institutions may submit PhD candidates who held graduate-level scholarships in the past. Candidates with dual nationality where one nationality is French are not eligible.

The eligible subject areas are the seven thematic areas listed under programmes. The funded study period must start between 1 September and 30 November of the award year, and the start date cannot be postponed.

An Eiffel scholarship cannot be combined with another French government scholarship, an Erasmus+ scholarship or a scholarship from the Agence Universitaire de la Francophonie; a person holding two must decline one.
age_experience_notes: Up to 29 years old for master's candidates and up to 35 years old for doctoral candidates. No work experience requirement is stated.
funding_summary: Master's recipients get a monthly allowance of 1,200 and doctoral recipients 2,000 (amounts effective 1 January 2026; the regulations show no currency symbol). Funding lasts up to 12 months for a second-year master's (M2), up to 24 months for a first-year master's (M1), up to 36 months for an engineering programme, and 12, 18 or 36 months for a doctorate. Besides the allowance, the programme gives airfare reimbursement (up to 50% of the ministry's maximum rate for the country), domestic travel to the study location, health insurance, housing help and cultural activities. Tuition and course fees are not paid by the programme, but holders of a French government scholarship are exempt from tuition fees for national degrees at public institutions under the higher education ministry.
programmes_note: Seven thematic areas are eligible. In technical and exact sciences: Biology and Health; Ecological Transition; Mathematics and Digital Technology; Engineering Sciences. In humanities and social sciences: French History, Language, and Civilization; Law and Political Science; Economics and Management. The scholarship is awarded for the specific programme named in the application at the institution that submitted it. The programme can be changed during studies only if the new one is in the same field and at the same institution; otherwise payments are suspended immediately.
institutions_note: Applications come from French higher education institutions and national research organisations. The brochure says nearly 400 partner institutions take part. Institutions that took part before receive an email giving access to the application platform; first-time institutions must contact the Eiffel programme team at Campus France to get the application files. No fixed list of institutions is published on the pages read; students choose an institution that fits their plans and ask it to nominate them.

summary.detail: Master's degree (or equivalent) accredited by the French state, or a nationally accredited engineering programme. Funding of up to 12 months when entering M2, up to 24 months when entering M1, up to 36 months when entering an engineering programme. Monthly allowance 1,200 (from 1 January 2026). Candidates up to 29 years old; those already studying in France are ineligible. One extra month of funding from August is possible for language training before the programme, only if it is mentioned in the application; its cost is the student's own. Teaching language is not stated by the sources.

summary.detail: Doctoral programme run as a dual degree or under joint supervision of the dissertation with a partner institution abroad. Funding of 12, 18 or 36 months counted from 1 September of the award year: 36 months only for new candidates entering the first year of a doctorate and not already studying in France; up to 18 months for those entering the first or second year; up to 12 months for those entering the second or third year. Stays in France can be split (not for 36-month awards), each funded stay at least 6 months, total not more than 3 years. Monthly allowance 2,000 (from 1 January 2026). Candidates up to 35 years old; those living abroad have priority over those living in France. A doctoral contract with employee status is not compatible with the scholarship.

benefits.limit_text: 1,200 per month at master's level; 2,000 per month at doctoral level (effective 1 January 2026; the regulations show no currency symbol)
benefits.conditions: Paid by bank transfer to an account in France in the recipient's name; the first payment is sent by Western Union. The first instalment needs the recipient to have started studies at the host institution. Paid from the day of arrival (not earlier than the agreed arrival date) and only while the recipient is at the specified location. Suspended during an optional internship or exchange, a gap year, or a repeated year. Master's: up to 12, 24 or 36 months depending on entry year or engineering programme; doctorate: 12, 18 or 36 months.

benefits.limit_text: Least-expensive airfare between the airport closest to home and the study location in France, reimbursed on receipts up to 50% of the ministry's maximum rate for that country; plus second-class train or bus travel from the arrival airport to the study location
benefits.conditions: Return flight (same 50% cap, plus second-class train or bus to the airport) must be requested within 12 months of the end of the scholarship and depends on Campus France receiving the final-year academic results.

benefits.limit_text: Temporary health insurance arranged by Campus France until French national health scheme cover starts, then supplementary health insurance at no cost to the recipient
benefits.conditions: The national scheme is compulsory and free for students enrolled in a French institution. Proof of enrolment must reach Campus France within two months of arrival; payments may be suspended if it is missing by the start of the third month. EU recipients with a European Health Insurance Card send a copy to be enrolled in the supplementary plan. Accompanying family members are excluded.

benefits.limit_text: Campus France offers a place in a CROUS student residence or in a private home; the recipient may decline and find their own housing
benefits.conditions: The brochure lists a housing allowance among the covered items, but the regulations describe housing help and offers only; no housing amount is stated. Housing provided by Campus France must be left when the scholarship is suspended or ends.

benefits.limit_text: Tuition and fees are not paid by the Eiffel programme at master's or doctoral level
benefits.conditions: Holders of a French government scholarship are exempt from tuition fees for a national degree or the engineer diploma at public institutions under the higher education ministry. Course fees are not covered. Language training before the programme is at the student's own cost.

benefits.limit_text: Cultural and leisure activities: weekend outings, 3-4 day trips and shorter events offered at student-friendly prices; membership of the Eiffel alumni community
benefits.conditions: Brochure also mentions no visa fees where applicable and support throughout the stay.

requirements.text: Application file for the nominated candidate, filled in and submitted online by the French institution on the Campus France application platform. The pages read do not list the documents inside the file.
After the award: place of residence
After the award: email address and telephone number
After the award: certificate of academic enrolment for the current year, sent as soon as the programme begins
After the award: proof of enrolment in the French national health insurance scheme (or the European Health Insurance Card for EU students), within two months of arrival

After the award: twice a year, two forms filled in and signed by the institution: an evaluation form at the end of the first semester and a performance report at the end of the year (for doctoral candidates, a report from the doctoral committee)

application_steps.title: Get in touch with Campus France and a French institution
application_steps.detail: Contact the Campus France office in your country, or the cooperation and cultural service of the French embassy, to discuss your study plan. Then contact the international relations office of a French institution about its application procedure and deadline. Students cannot send applications directly.

application_steps.title: The institution accepts you and nominates you
application_steps.detail: The institution must accept your candidacy and support it. Returning institutions get an email giving access to the application files; first-time institutions contact the Eiffel programme team at Campus France. Applications submitted by students or foreign institutions are declared ineligible.

application_steps.title: The institution submits the file before the January deadline
application_steps.detail: For the 2027 session the call opens in October 2026 and Campus France must receive the institution's applications by 6 January 2027 (inclusive). The brochure describes the same pattern: online call, deadline in the first week of January. If language training before the programme is wanted, it must be written in the application file.

application_steps.title: Expert panels review the nominated candidates
application_steps.detail: A selection commission made up of seven panels of experts, one per field of study, chooses the awardees. The brochure names the criteria: the candidate's record of excellence, the institution's reputation abroad and international student policy, and its cooperation and partnership policy with the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. Candidates are first pre-selected by their institution.

application_steps.title: Results are published from 12 April 2027
application_steps.detail: Campus France page gives results from 12 April 2027. The brochure, an older general document, says March; the dated 2027 page is the one to follow. Individual candidates are informed through their institution; the pages read do not describe the notification step in detail.

application_steps.title: Enrol and start studies between 1 September and 30 November
application_steps.detail: The recipient must be officially enrolled at the French institution that submitted the application, and the funded period must begin between 1 September and 30 November 2027. The start date cannot be postponed. The first allowance instalment is paid only after studies begin.

application_steps.title: Send enrolment and health insurance proof to Campus France
application_steps.detail: Send the certificate of academic enrolment as soon as the programme begins, and proof of enrolment in the French national health scheme within two months of arrival. Recipients get a personal online space, Mon Espace Boursier, to upload documents, update contact details and track payments and requests.

application_steps.title: Keep to the rules during the award
application_steps.detail: Sit all exams and follow the institution's rules; report academic progress twice a year. Tell Campus France in advance before an internship abroad (agreement at least one week before), travel abroad or a gap year (request at least 2 months ahead, one gap year of exactly one year at most). Repeating a year suspends the scholarship; signing an apprenticeship or professionalisation contract ends it. Publications must acknowledge the French ministry's support. Recipients who break the rules may have to repay the scholarship and the cost of services received.

application_steps.title: Request the return ticket within 12 months of the end
application_steps.detail: Ask for the return flight within 12 months of the scholarship ending; it depends on Campus France receiving the final-year academic results. Recipients then join the Eiffel alumni community and can register with the France Alumni network.
